newsitem.title: USA: Wash.'s $425 mln stadium passes,vote counting ends.
newsitem.headline: Wash.'s $425 mln stadium passes,vote counting ends.

text.p: A $425 million football stadium measure in Washington state was narrowly approved by voters with a 36,780 ballot margin, according to final unofficial election results released on Wednesday.
Stadium supporters, backed by billionaire Paul Allen, won the cliffhanger election with 820,364 'yes' votes. A total of 783,584 'no' votes were recorded, the state said.
The final results will be certified Thursday by state election officials.

The measure will provide about $325 million in public money for a 72,000-seat open-air stadium to house the Seattle Seahawks. Allen, co-founder of Microsoft Corp and owner of the NBA Portland Trail Blazers, would invest an additional $100 million in the project.

Allen, worth more than $13 billion, offered to buy the Seahawks -- but only if the stadium referendum was approved. The new stadium, which would open in 2002, would replace the aging Kingdome, an indoor facility that would be demolished.

The stadium financing package will include $101 million from existing sales taxes, $127 million from lottery games, $56 million in stadium admissions and parking taxes, and $40 million in hotel room taxes.
The state will issue up to $300 million of bonds to pay for site acquisition, design and construction of the stadium and an exhibition center.
